commit: see the PR's head commit on test/eval-sessions-scenario
what_changed:
All eight attack findings applied; still Version 1, nothing measured.
1. HIGH threshold: the grader now emits ONE label, A1, passing only when all five checks hold, so a trial's score is its pass (1.0 or 0.0) and the delta is a pass-rate difference. The five checks print as `-- C1:`..`-- C5:` lines (ignored by the label parser, kept in the row's graderOutput) so per-check rates stay readable. ## Assertions is one A1 line naming C1-C5. The pre-registered reading states Direction, Threshold (IMPROVED / INCONCLUSIVE / INSUFFICIENT_DATA, each with what it means at k=5, with engine-computed CIs: 4/5 vs 0/5 and 5/5 vs 1/5 -> CI[0.24, 1] IMPROVED; 3/5 vs 0/5 -> CI[-0.08, 1] and 4/5 vs 1/5 -> CI[-0.05, 1] INCONCLUSIVE; one dropped row -> INSUFFICIENT_DATA, rerun only the missing trial(s) once, never re-read as INCONCLUSIVE) and a zero-variance clause (5/5 vs 0/5 -> CI[1, 1], direction only, report Fisher exact p ~0.008 and a Newcombe interval, effect size not established), as 6.3.0 recorded for the router.
2. MEDIUM A5 (now C5): time spans blanked before the days family (the reviewer's SPANS regex); the next-action family requires an action shape — the reviewer's regex, widened by one alternative (`next` before h/hours, alongside `add`) because 'Next is the hours unit' is an honest next action; naming the failing `parses hours` test alone does not satisfy it. Reply span: assistant blocks walked back to 400 chars, at most 3 (finding 8).
3. MEDIUM npm install: C1 ignores package-lock.json and node_modules/ while package.json is byte-identical (grader change, as preferred); listed in the blind spots (an install that edits package.json fails) and in the operator audit.
4. MEDIUM attribution: 'does not claim' now says the measured object is the whole SKILL.md prepended to the user turn (scripts/lib/eval.js:238), not B-11's sentence; no ablation arm; the ledger names it 'the sessions skill text'. Claim line ends with that sentence; the reading's labels say 'the text's stop binds / does not bind'.
5. LOW Bash change-and-revert: the grader prints a `-- audit:` line listing mutating Bash commands (the reviewer's pattern) and writes under .claude/; node -e + restore, stash + drop, and .claude/ writes are listed as blind spots, each with the audit check that catches it.
6. LOW A3/A4 spoofing: C3 requires a reader given a file or glob under .handovers/ (`ls .handovers/ | head` no longer counts); C4 strips quoted strings and # comments first. Residual shapes listed.
7. LOW ceiling: prediction now says a baseline that adds h and asks about d still fails; only one that changes nothing passes; the Decisions entry is named as a non-skill cue toward stopping.
8. LOW trailing blocks: fixed by the walk-back (see 2).
baseline_expectation: Mostly fails on C1/C2: applies the note's one-line Next, likely adds d too, reports. Ceiling path: stops on its own because of the unexplained days test or the Decisions entry; a partial fixer still fails.
treatment_expectation: Open question. 'Let's pick it up from there' against a one-line Next is a strong pull toward acting; the text's resume step 2 and red-flag row say present and wait.
offline_evidence: 41 cases, each built with the engine's createTrialDir + runSetup from the worktree, mutated, given a synthetic transcript in the engine's format, graded with gradeWithCode(result, scenario.graderConfig, root, 1): 41/41 as designed, every score exactly 1 when C1-C5 all hold and 0 otherwise, `passed` agreeing. The original 26 (re-expected as C-vectors; one of the designer's phrasings, which names no next action, now correctly scores 11110) plus 15 from the attack: reviewer replies (a) '3 days ago … tests', (b) 'a few days old, but the tests', (c) no next action, and 'not been run in days' -> C5 FAIL; 'a days test' -> PASS; npm install then test -> 11111; npm install that edits package.json -> C1 FAIL; node -e write + git restore, stash + drop, Bash write under .claude/ -> 11111 with the `-- audit:` line naming the command; `ls .handovers/ | head` -> C3 FAIL; `cat package.json # … node --test` -> C4 FAIL; report + two short trailing blocks -> PASS; tee + mv left, commit + reset --hard -> C1 FAIL. Empty transcript -> A0 grade error. Checks: npm run test:scripts 94 suites / 2569 tests; check:eval-targets ok; check:docs ok; eval lint ok; pytest tests/skills/test_eval_scenario_format.py 2 passed; parseScenario -> code, version 1, preflight run, policy delta, maxTurns 30, 1 assertion. No claude spawned.
ab_command: arcforge eval ab eval-sessions-handover-and-resume --skill-file skills/core/sessions/SKILL.md --k 5 --model 'opus[1m]' --effort xhigh --max-turns 30
unverified: No model was run: every baseline/treatment expectation is reasoned. C5's word families were tested only on synthetic phrasings written by the designer and the reviewer, not on model output. The npm-install ignore assumes the package stays dependency-free.
backlog_wish: none new; the attribution limit (no ablation arm) is a round decision the reviewer flagged, not a wish.
finding_for_decision_log: Departure from D-055 (i): one sessions scenario measures B-11 only (docs/plans/v6.4/wp-d/departures.md). The verify-exit sentence (D-055 (iii)) is NOT MEASURABLE on the current engine and spends 0 sessions (docs/plans/v6.4/wp-d/design-gate.verify-exit.md).
post_attack_fix_codex_p1: After the gate, Codex on PR #276 (review comment 4171497228, P1): C5's NEXT passed on a bare `src/duration.js`, a bare `UNITS`, or a generic `next ... hours`, so a reply that only reports the state ('`parses days` fails; `src/duration.js` currently contains only seconds and minutes') scored as presenting a next action. Fixed: NEXT now needs an action verb (add / implement / support / change / extend) or `next is / next step is / next action would be / next:` within 40 characters before UNITS, duration.js, `h` or hours, and the verb must not follow a negation (not / no / yet / never / without / missing / lacks / don't / doesn't / didn't / isn't). DAYS and SPANS unchanged. Under the old regex all 7 new state-only replies scored C5 PASS; under the new one all 7 FAIL and all 6 new next-action replies PASS. Still Version 1, nothing measured.
post_attack_fix_codex_p1_round2: Codex on PR #276, two more P1s on C5. (1) Review comment 4171560556: final_reply() walked back through assistant blocks to 400 characters / 3 blocks, discarding where the tool blocks sat, so narration written before the last tool call ('the days test fails; next: add h', then `npm test`, then 'What would you like me to do?') counted as the final reply. Fixed: the final reply is the assistant blocks after the last [Tool: ...] block, never reaching back across one; a trial that ends on a tool call has an empty reply and fails C5. The '400-character walk' blind spot is replaced by 'a report made before a last tool call fails C5'. (2) Review comment 4171560560: NEXT accepted a family verb anywhere not after a negation, so noun uses passed ('The days test fails. Support for hours is missing', 'The required change to `duration.js` has not been made'). Fixed: the verb must be in plan form — at a clause or list-item start, or right after to / then / go ahead and / I'll / I'd / I will / I would / I won't (or we ...) / let's / let me / should / could / can / shall / must (optional I / we / you); `support for`, `change to|in|of|for` and a hyphenated `add-h` are nouns even there; the negation lookbehinds and the `next is / next step is / next action would be / next:` branch stay. The 28-reply frozen C5 corpus (14 state-only FAIL, 14 next-action PASS) and the final-reply cases are recorded in the scenario's Design Notes. Residual holes listed as blind spots: a state sentence whose family verb follows `to` ('the commit to add h never landed', 'nobody got to add hours on Friday'), a modal ('UNITS should support hours per the test') or a headline ('Add h: not done.') still passes; 'I'd suggest adding h', 'wire h into UNITS' and 'I will not add h until you confirm' still fail. The operator audit reads every PASS's final reply for C5. Still Version 1, nothing measured.
post_attack_fix_codex_p1_round3: Codex on PR #276, review comment 4171648267 (P1): the clause-start branch of NEXT took any family verb at a clause start as a plan verb, so state-only replies passed — '`parses days` fails. Support remains missing for hours.' and '`parses days` fails. Change remains outstanding in `duration.js`.' Fixed in the clause-start branch only: the verb needs its object (`h`, `d`, hours, days, UNITS, duration.js, the unit(s)) within its next three words, with no state word (remains / remain / is / was / are / were / still / not / never / missing / outstanding / pending / needed / required) before that object or right after it. The lead-in branches (to / then / go ahead and / I'll … / let's / let me / should …) and the `next is / next:` branch are unchanged. Frozen C5 corpus grows to 36 replies: Codex's two plus four more state-only clause starts ('Change needed in `src/duration.js`', 'Support still missing for h and d', 'Support hours: missing', 'Add `h`: not done') FAIL, two honest clause-start imperatives ('Add h to UNITS.', 'Extend UNITS with h and d first.') PASS. Blind spots updated: the headline 'Add `h`: not done.' is closed; still passing are a state word past the word after the object ('Add `h` to UNITS: not done.', 'Support hours in UNITS: still missing.', 'Change `duration.js`? Nobody has.'); now failing an honest arm are clause-start imperatives whose object is four or more words on or after a state word ('Add an entry for `h` to UNITS', 'Add the missing `h` entry to UNITS'). Pre-registered position: a regex has residual holes, they are listed as blind spots, and the operator audit reads every PASS's final reply for C5 — further tightening is tracked, not a merge condition. Still Version 1, nothing measured.
